cycle_intent: retry_measurement (driver-initiated frozen replay of cycle 10, final attempt 2/2) + a harness investigation/fix pass before the replay
summary: Investigated the ~70s per-arm wall budget that has blocked test_data_scaleup_v1 (smoke=12) screening for two cycles running (c10, c11). Root cause: decode compute, not budget arithmetic. _arm_wall_minutes already splits the immovable MAX_RUN_MINUTES=3-derived ceiling (155s minus a 15s finalization reserve) as tightly as possible into two symmetric 70s arms; decode_progress.json telemetry from c10/c11/c12 (three independent measurements) converges tightly on ~14.2-14.3s/record, >97% of which is compiler_ms (grammar-constrained forward-symbol-table passes in the decode compiler). 12 smoke records need ~172s of pure decode -- about 2.5x the entire two-arm wall budget, before any training or I/O overhead. No redistribution of the fixed arm budget closes that deficit. What was fixable and safe within autoresearch/experiments-family harness scope: nothing previously stopped a *new* (non-frozen) screening/promotion cycle from silently defaulting onto an eval snapshot whose suites cannot plausibly complete a decode pass in one arm. Added _feasible_eval_version (scripts/run_autotrain_continuous.py, commit 14ec931) to estimate role-required suite decode time from the measured per-record cost and fall through _DEFAULT_EVAL_VERSION_CANDIDATES to the first candidate that fits, with regression tests. This guard does not and cannot affect the already-frozen c10 replay chain (frozen replays reuse the exact locked eval_version by design), so the mandatory retry_measurement action from c11's handoff was still consumed this cycle exactly as before -- and it still hit wall_timeout, exactly as predicted by the root-cause analysis.

budget_investigation.conclusion: decode compute bound, not a budget-arithmetic bug -- no safe reallocation of the fixed 70s arm makes 12 records fit; ~4 records/arm is the theoretical ceiling at this measured decode rate (untested at n=4/5, not attempted -- would only be a marginal 33% gain over the already-tested n=3 fixture and was judged not worth a new quality-gated data publish for that little signal).

harness_fix.change: scripts/run_autotrain_continuous.py: added _suite_record_count, _eval_version_fits_arm_budget, _feasible_eval_version; call site at eval_version selection now uses _feasible_eval_version(role=role, arm_wall_minutes=arm_wall_minutes, policy=policy) instead of the unfiltered default_eval_version().
harness_fix.scope_note: test_data_scaleup_v1 was never durably added to engine.py's _DEFAULT_EVAL_VERSION_CANDIDATES (c10/c11 used a non-tracked runtime monkeypatch because editing engine.py drags in the pre-existing, unrelated-to-this-loop broken test_continuous_classify_positive_entry via the check-changed pre-commit hook's src/slm_training/autoresearch/ -> tests/test_autoresearch mapping). This cycle's fix deliberately lives entirely in scripts/run_autotrain_continuous.py (maps only to tests/test_scripts under check_changed.py) so it commits cleanly without touching or depending on that broken test.
